text: When three events repeat at different intervals, the first time they all coincide is related to a concept from basic number theory. What operation on two numbers gives you the smallest number that both divide into evenly?
A regular function computes everything at once and returns a result. But what if a function could pause, hand you one value, and resume where it left off when you ask for the next one?
The keyword 'yield' turns a function into something different something that remembers its state between calls and produces values one at a time. What is this called?

To measure how much memory a data structure uses, Python has a function in the sys module. Compare the memory of a list with a million items to the memory of a generator that can produce a million items.
To run three independent loops simultaneously, look at the threading module. To make threads wait for each other at specific points, look at threading.Event one thread signals, others wait.
